name: CPU scheduling
title: Who gets the CPU next?
work: The C port implements FIFO, SJF and round robin, explicit/random job lists, execution traces and per-job response, turnaround and waiting statistics. The archive also contains the OSTEP Python reference and eleven scheduling answer/trace files.
scope: All jobs arrive at time zero, use CPU only, and pay no context-switch cost here. Explicit positive integer lists are supported. The browser does not reproduce the C/Python random generators or every CLI formatting detail.

name: Feedback & lottery
title: A policy can change the queue.
work: The archived MLFQ answers explore queue levels, quanta, boosts and I/O behavior using OSTEP's supplied simulator. Lottery C/Python teaching examples show ticket-based selection.
scope: This new MLFQ model has CPU-only jobs, three queues and quanta 1/2/4. It omits arrival and I/O rules. Lottery draws use a browser LCG, not C random() or Python random. Finite shares fluctuate; ticket proportions are expectations.

name: Managed heap
title: See the space between allocations.
work: hashproj.c adds an mmap-backed managed heap, first-fit allocation, headers, free-list insertion and coalescing. Later code adapts the allocator to a malloc-backed heap shared by threads and protected by a mutex.
scope: The visual allocator is a newly written, corrected reference with a 256-byte heap, 16-byte alignment and 16-byte allocation headers. It illustrates splitting/coalescing without executing or silently repairing the archived allocator.

name: Block hasher
title: Bytes become a tree, then a signature.
work: The source reads 1,024-byte blocks, counts byte frequencies, constructs a Huffman tree, hashes a preorder traversal and adds block signatures modulo 2,147,483,647. Fork mode returns child results through pipes.
scope: The browser ports the supplied heap tie rules and tree signature arithmetic for up to 4,096 UTF-8 bytes. It models the algorithm, not allocator layout, forks or native memory faults. This is a faux educational signature, not a cryptographic file hash.

name: Concurrency
title: Shared state needs a deliberate order.
work: sharedhash.c and esharedhash.c add pthread workers, result slots and a mutex-protected allocator. The experimental version joins batches after up to 16 active worker creations. The archive also covers condition variables, semaphores and concurrency bugs.
scope: The counter interleaving below is a new teaching example, not a race observed in the submitted hasher. Manual events demonstrate lost updates and mutex exclusion. No real threads, timings or OS scheduler are running.

name: Optimization report
title: Compare the evidence, not just the headline.
work: The report redirects Huffman-related allocations through halloc/hfree to malloc/free under EXPERIMENTAL_ALLOC, while block buffers still use the custom allocator. It records matching signatures and a wall-time reduction from 3.839 s to 0.432 s.
scope: These are archived timings, not newly measured benchmarks. Another screenshot records 3.381 s versus 0.464 s. Matching weak signatures on one input support a regression check, not a proof of universal correctness or a measured lock-contention percentage.

name: Memory & persistence
title: An address and a write both need a plan.
work: Course materials cover address translation, paging, TLBs, swapping, files, storage devices, RAID and crash consistency. The archive separates instructor solution PDFs from project implementations.
scope: The page-table and journaling models are new conceptual exercises. They do not claim to be submitted code or a real virtual-memory/filesystem implementation. Page size, frames and log ordering are explicit teaching assumptions.

name: Source & review
title: Keep every stage inspectable.
tag: 189 files / eight code files / eleven answer records
work: The original ZIP contains the project sources, scaffolds/reference scripts, scheduling traces, experiment report/evidence, binary test fixtures, lecture decks, textbook chapters and instructor solutions. Every file is inventoried with its role and duplicate relationships.
scope: Read-only source viewers preserve text with normalized line endings. Prebuilt executables are inventoried but never run or redistributed. Fresh C builds were used only for bounded local checks. Not every long answer trace or reference slide is independently certified.
